title: Language Services Standard: Interpreter Lead Time for First Hearings in Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
American Sign Language, another language, or Spanish: when an appeal's first hearing is set under Unemployment Insurance Appeals, the *first-setting interpreter lead* is decided by the latest interpreter request on the appeal — the request with the most recent request date.

**Standard.** The first-setting interpreter lead is the sign-language lead days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for American Sign Language, the contract-interpreter lead days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for a language other than American Sign Language and Spanish, and zero days when the latest interpreter request is for Spanish or no interpreter is requested. The first hearing date found from the first-setting clock and the first-setting target is moved later by this lead before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied.

| Latest interpreter request on the appeal | First-setting interpreter lead |
|---|---|
| American Sign Language | 10 calendar days (sign-language lead) |
| any language other than American Sign Language and Spanish | 7 calendar days (contract-interpreter lead) |
| Spanish | 0 days |
| no interpreter requested | 0 days |

## Points of judgement

- Only the latest request counts. Earlier requests on the same appeal, for whatever language, do not add to it.
- The lead is in calendar days and is added to the first hearing date found from the clock and the target, ahead of the notice minimum and the weekend rule.

## Hypothetical requests on one appeal

| Requests on the appeal (by request date) | Latest | Lead |
|---|---|---|
| Spanish on 1 April, then American Sign Language on 8 April | American Sign Language | 10 days |
| American Sign Language on 1 April, then Spanish on 8 April | Spanish | 0 days |
| Tagalog on 3 April | Tagalog | 7 days |
| none | — | 0 days |

*Worked illustration (hypothetical):* the first hearing date found from the clock and the target is Monday 4 May 2026 and the latest request is for Tagalog. The date moves 7 days later, to Monday 11 May, before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied.
